lesson_title: Why 1 m³ Is a Million cm³
hook_text: How many sugar-cube-sized blocks fill a 1 m box? Not 100. A million.
clip_script: One cubic metre is a cube one hundred centimetres by one hundred by one hundred: one hundred times one hundred times one hundred, 1 000 000 cubic centimetres — one million. Picture building the metre cube from centimetre cubes: a bottom layer of 10 000, and one hundred such layers.
visual_style: A one-metre box fills with tiny cubes layer by layer; a counter races to 10 000 for the first layer then 1 000 000; water pours in labelled 1 kl.
pacing: Layer fill accelerates, million reveal, water link.
call_to_action: Watch the full lesson to convert between every unit of volume and capacity.
